name: Target-tier gate: every grant gate needs its revoke/demote mirror
description: Phase 6.5's hybrid gates bounded only the role being GRANTED (actor > candidate, senior subset verdict) — and removeMember took no actor at all. Pre-6.5 unreachable (every manage holder sat at/above all non-owner targets); the senior tier is the FIRST below-tier manage holder, making 'senior demotes/removes an administrator' a live escalation (deep-review Critical, fixed in 136e826). The gate: acting ON an existing member (changeRole/removeMember) rejects when the target's CURRENT role_level is strictly above the actor's (422 ROLE_SUBSET_VIOLATION). Pinned semantics: peers stay manageable (admin removes a peer admin — the pre-6.5 cell, preserved); an unreadable TARGET level never outranks (revocation only NARROWS access, and a member holding a corrupted role must stay removable — the deliberate asymmetry with the strict actor-side levelOf); DELETE resolves the actor from the authenticated subject (no body). General rule: whenever a slice introduces a new tier or capability holder BELOW an existing tier, the revoke/demote/unassign mirror of every grant gate becomes reachable and needs its own QA row.

B4 deep-review M1. The user-service /internal/** is kept off the gateway by OMISSION — its APISIX pool only has /api/v1/teams* + /api/v1/users* routes, so /internal/* simply has nowhere to match. That reasoning is SOUND only for a pool whose routes are all explicit prefixes. The CATALOG pool, however, is served by a catch-all route (uri=/*, priority 0) — so when B4 T6 added GET /internal/catalog/{id}/created-by (app-side permitAll('/internal/**'), in-network-by-design), the catch-all happily matched and proxied it, leaking the catalog creator sub to any authenticated caller through the gateway. Three in-code comments asserted 'never gateway-fronted'; all three were false for catalog. The gateway opa plugin is the allow-all 'gateway' placeholder, so it did not block it either.
resolution: Make the invariant STRUCTURAL, not incidental: add an explicit deny route ABOVE the catch-all rather than relying on a missing route. infra/apisix/init-routes.sh now defines route 'internal-blocked' (uri=/internal/*, priority 70 > usermgmt's 60 > the catch-all's 0) whose serverless-pre-function (already enabled in config.yaml) does core.response.exit(404) before any upstream is selected. GENERAL RULE: whenever a pool is fronted by a catch-all (/*), every in-network-only path (/internal/**, actuator, etc.) MUST be positively blocked at the edge — 'we didn't add a route for it' is not protection when a /* route exists. Verified live: all /internal/* -> 404, public /api/v1/* still route (302 oidc, not the block). Future: replace the allow-all gateway.rego with a real coarse policy and this becomes defense-in-depth rather than the sole edge guard.

title: Demo/e2e teams must bind a SYSTEM-ladder role to be manageable — custom roles are management-incapable by design
rationale: ADR 0015 §5 pins it: the control plane (team:add-member/change-role/remove-member/define-roles/transfer) is carried ONLY by reserved system codes (owner/administrator/senior); a custom role projects to READ-only on type:team regardless of stored permissions. Consequence for ANY seeded/bootstrapped team: binding only custom roles produces a team NO member can manage — the SPA picker's add-member 403s for everyone (found in the USER-DIRECTORY-PORT browser verify; the seed's flagship demo team had exactly this). Fix shape: bind the admin persona as 'owner' via the membership bootstrap (ensureMembership resolves system codes first and UPSERTS the role on an existing (team,user) row, so a re-seed converges a role change in place). Rejected alternative: hiding/degrading the picker's controls client-side — contradicts the pinned optimistic-controls posture (ADR 0016 §8: show the action, let the server's typed denial tell the story). Also: seeds that promise a reproducible baseline should RESET their team's roster to the canonical members (scoped DELETE by team_id) — stale-subject memberships accumulate across Keycloak realm re-imports (every re-create mints new subs, orphaning old rows).

title: Action-enrichment verb sets verified against real endpoints, not assumed (caught 2 corrections)
rationale: Phase-6 00-DESIGN listed catalog/product expected abacActions=[view,update,delete,assign-tags] with a 'verify in setup' caveat. The decompose-time endpoint scout proved catalog AND product have NO assign-tags endpoint (neither carries tags) — so both sets are [view,update,delete]; only category keeps assign-tags. assign-roles is structurally unreachable for catalog resources (role assignment is team:change-role in user-mgmt; the rego tests confirm even the editor realm role can't reach category:assign-roles) — never enumerate it. team enriches ONLY the OPA-fully-decided subset [list-members,add-member,remove-member]; the 6.7 Java-co-gated verbs (change-role/define-roles/transfer-ownership) are excluded by affordance-honesty (OPA alone says true but the MembershipService escalation gate + owner-only-by-code fence decide the specific attempt). Also: user-mgmt getTeam is UNGATED (owner-on-create bootstrap), so a Team is never gate-cached -> its _actions cache-misses and is omitted (the visible degrade, a correct outcome, not a bug). The general rule: an enrichment registry must enumerate only verbs that (a) have a real per-instance endpoint AND (b) are wholly OPA-decided; enumerating an unreachable or Java-co-gated verb makes the affordance map lie (perpetual-false or over-promise->4xx). Verify against the live @OpaPreAuthorize annotations before pinning the set — the same fail-closed discipline that drops assign-roles.

name: createTeam squat-gate: structural bootstrap bypass + production-must-enable-or-deny-all
description: B4 T7 (ADR 0019) wires the ResourceOwnershipResolver into the PUBLIC TeamController.createTeam: requireOwnership(targetType,targetId) gets the caller's raw sub (CallerIdentity.currentSubject() — NEW, distinct from currentUserId() the internal profile id; ownership is keyed by the sub = the catalog's created_by) + the resolver via ObjectProvider; isOwner false / resolver ABSENT / no subject -> throw NotResourceOwnerException -> 403 ACCESS_DENIED (the SAME library code an @OpaPreAuthorize deny yields, so a squat is indistinguishable from any authz failure; the exception message names only the target, never the owner). TWO load-bearing design points: (1) the /internal/bootstrap/teams seed path BYPASSES the gate BY CONSTRUCTION — it's a SEPARATE controller (InternalBootstrapController) that never calls createTeam, so there is NO 'skip ownership' boolean to misconfigure on the public path (the B2 lesson: the off-ramp would be the vuln). I9 proves it bypasses even with a denying decision. (2) FAIL-CLOSED DEFAULT BITES IN PROD: because abac.ownership.enabled defaults OFF, a user-service deployed WITHOUT it (or without the catalog registry entry) fails EVERY public createTeam to 403. So the rig/prod MUST set abac.ownership.enabled=true + abac.ownership.services.catalog=http://catalog:8080 on the user-service or self-service create is dead (T9 rig config). TEST BACK-COMPAT: existing HTTP-path createTeam ITs would all 403 (resolver absent) — fix is a @Primary test ResourceOwnershipResolver in AbacTestConfig delegating to a settable static ownershipDecision (default owner-of-everything; OwnershipGateIT overrides per cell + resets @AfterEach). OwnerOnCreateIT is UNAFFECTED — it calls teamService.createWithOwner directly (service, not controller), below the gate. Existing e2e matrices create teams via /internal/bootstrap/teams (the bypass), so E8 unaffected. Relates: uq_team_target (T3) already blocks a SECOND team on a target; this guards the FIRST create on a catalog you didn't create.

title: 6.7 resolve-side: team management ladder stays a Java projection (TeamRoleCapabilities recast to category tokens), custom roles management-incapable
rationale: 6.7 phase-① (2026-06-15). DISCOVERY: seeded system roles store category tokens under the WILDCARD '*' key ({owner/admin: [READ,WRITE,TAG,GRANT]}, senior/member: [READ,WRITE,TAG], reader: [READ]) — these are RESOURCE perms (resourceRole expands '*' -> target type). The TEAM MANAGEMENT ladder is a SEPARATE, narrower, code-driven projection (admin's mgmt = read/manage/define-tags, NOT its resource GRANT) synthesized by TeamRoleCapabilities.forCode — it CANNOT be read from the stored '*' tokens because the two sets deliberately differ (owner's define-roles/transfer-ownership have no resource analog). So the mgmt ladder stays a JAVA PROJECTION, recast from fine verbs to CATEGORY TOKENS: owner/administrator -> [READ, CONTROL, TAG]; senior -> [READ, CONTROL]; member/reader -> [READ]; custom code -> [READ] (the I12 fence). managementRole keeps shape Map.of('team', forCode(code)); team.rego expands those tokens via the SHARED data.permission_categories (single expansion home, symmetric with catalog.rego). Owner-only fences (define-roles, transfer-ownership) are NOT in the token map — enforced by team.rego's owner-by-code rule. CUSTOM ROLES stay management-incapable (Option A, I12 'ceiling != capability' preserved): managementRole projects custom codes to READ-only on type:team regardless of stored permissions; validateContract TIGHTENED to reject CONTROL (and team-meaningful TAG) tokens under the 'team' key for custom roles — turning today's silent dead-data into an explicit 422. Rejected moving the ladder into OPA data (would create a 2nd table, break single-expansion-home). Rejected opening custom-role team power (separate bigger escalation analysis, would bloat the slice).

name: Pluggable cross-service ownership: config-registry discovery + (type,id) cache, fail-closed
description: B4 T5 (ADR 0019): ResourceOwnershipResolver SPI (opa-abac-spring-security, NOT core — no Spring Data type) closes target-squatting for self-service createTeam. boolean isOwner(subject, resourceType, UUID resourceId), type-keyed, FAIL-CLOSED: false on EVERY non-affirmative outcome (unknown type / unreachable / 404 / 5xx / blank-or-malformed body / mismatch / null coords), and NEVER throws past its boundary (a throw a caller might catch-and-allow would re-open squatting). Default impl DiscoveryOwnershipResolver: a config-driven type->base-URL registry (@ConfigurationProperties abac.ownership.services.<type>=<url>) — adding an owning service is ONE config line + that service implementing the standard contract GET /internal/{type}/{id}/created-by -> 200 {createdBy:sub} / 404, no per-service code dependency (the decoupling win vs point-to-point). The resolver does the compare (createdBy.equals(subject)), so the CACHE KEY is (type,id) — subject-INDEPENDENT -> good hit rate + doesn't leak which subject asked. CRITICAL cache rule: cache ONLY authoritative results (present-createdBy or resource-absent), NEVER a transient outage — else an outage pins a wrong answer for the whole TTL (pinned by outageNotCached_recoversOnNextCall). Injectable Clock for TTL (system in prod, virtual MutableClock in tests) so TTL expiry is asserted at virtual time, zero Thread.sleep — the B3 discipline (mx pattern). Starter wiring OwnershipAutoConfiguration: @ConditionalOnProperty(abac.ownership.enabled, default OFF) so catalog pays nothing + user-service opts in; @ConditionalOnMissingBean for adopter override; ObjectProvider<ObjectMapper>.getIfAvailable(ObjectMapper::new) so it wires in a bare ApplicationContextRunner slice too (the direct ObjectMapper inject failed the slice test). Consumer is T7 (createTeam: isOwner false -> 403; /internal/bootstrap bypasses). NOTE from T3: uq_team_target already blocks a SECOND team on an existing target; this check guards the FIRST team-create on a catalog you didn't create.

name: Team/role-def core: role≠grant entities, JSONB permissions, partial-unique role codes
description: user-management-service Phase-4 core domain. Four entities: User (principal, AbstractAuditableEntity, no tags), Team (AbstractSecuredEntity -> resource type 'team', carries team-target type+id with a unique constraint on (target_type,target_id) for resource->team indirection), RoleDefinitionEntity (the ROLE half; JSONB attributes + permissions in the {resourceType:[verbs]} shape the OPA policy reads; system flag + nullable teamId), TeamMembership (the GRANT half; unique (team_id,user_id), carries roleDefinitionId). Keep RoleDefinitionEntity named distinctly from the library's core.RoleDefinition record (decision/wire shape) to avoid a clash. System roles seeded by Liquibase with STABLE ids+codes mirrored in a SystemRoles constants class so app code resolves them without a query. System-role permissions use a wildcard '*' resource type (team-target-type-agnostic); the effective-role resolver expands '*' to the concrete team-target type. Role-code uniqueness needs TWO partial unique indexes in Postgres (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE team_id IS NULL for system roles vs WHERE team_id IS NOT NULL on (team_id,code) for custom) — authored via a Liquibase <sql splitStatements:true> block, not addUniqueConstraint.

name: Hierarchical resource authorization (inherit from parent)
description: When resources form a tree (Catalog -> Category -> Product), a child can inherit authorization from its parent. Resolve the parent chain and let a grant on an ancestor satisfy a check on a descendant. Make this an explicit, opt-in 'hierarchical' mode on the authorization API rather than implicit, so callers know when ancestor grants apply.

title: 6.7 proof obligations + behavior delta: counts RISE (not zero-Rego like B2), list-members loosening + custom-role 422 are the two intended behavior changes
rationale: 6.7 phase-① (2026-06-15) close-out. BASELINE: opa test infra 157, service-team 14. EXPECTED DELTA (pinned as direction+which-tests-change, NOT a magic number — decompose ② sets exact targets): infra RISES (~+8-12), service-team RISES (~20+). KNOWN INTENDED BREAK (the one a run could misread as regression): permissions_test.rego asserts READ=={view,list} at ~3 sites (lines 11-12,29-31,78) — these MUST update to {view,list,list-members}. ADD CONTROL expansion cases to permissions_test.rego. team_test.rego (BOTH copies) rewritten to the category model: every system code x every control verb, owner-only fence (define-roles/transfer-ownership allowed ONLY for code=='owner'), define-tags via TAG for owner/admin but NOT senior, unknown-token-denies, no-role-def-denies. MIRROR OBLIGATION: both permission_categories.json copies byte-identical after edit. TWO INTENDED EXTERNALLY-VISIBLE BEHAVIOR CHANGES (everything else is net-identical authorization, only wire-verb renames manage->add-member/change-role/remove-member): (1) list-members moves team:manage->READ so ANY team member can list the roster (today manager-only) — proof: member CAN GET /members AND member/reader still 403 on mutations+define-tags (loosening is EXACTLY listing); add a newman cell for it too. (2) validateContract now 422s a custom role carrying CONTROL/team-meaningful-TAG tokens under a 'team' key (was silent dead-data). NO DB/Liquibase migration — team ladder is a pure Java projection; system-role '*' resource seeds untouched. B2 tri-state supplier contract is a NON-GOAL (untouched). AUTONOMOUS-RUN RISK PINS (recurring planning-gap classes): the unpinned-fail-open-semantic class is covered by enumerating the full behavior delta above; the rig/two-copy gotcha class is covered by the mirror-both-bundles + both-team.rego-copies obligations + 'restart OPA after editing team.rego' (README) for any live e2e.

description: Testing the dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize path over a RANDOM_PORT TestRestTemplate: a test config that set the 'acting subject' via a ThreadLocal (AbacSubjectExtractor reads it) silently authenticated NOTHING — the in-process server runs the request on a Tomcat worker thread, not the JUnit test thread, so the ThreadLocal set in the test was invisible to the extractor. Symptom: deny-path tests pass (member/viewer 403) but allow-path tests fail (owner/admin get 403 too), because the subject was always empty -> fail-closed deny. Also hit a second wall: providing BOTH the app's production SecurityConfig chain AND a permissive test SecurityFilterChain throws 'a filter chain that matches any request has already been configured' (Spring Security 6.4 forbids two /** chains). And a FilterRegistrationBean<AbacFilter> with a null filter (when the starter is off and no AbacFilter bean exists) makes Tomcat throw 'Filter must not be null'.
resolution: Pass the acting identity IN THE REQUEST (a header the test AbacSubjectExtractor reads), never a ThreadLocal, so it travels with the HTTP call across threads. Use ONE security chain everywhere (the real SecurityConfig) and drive test permissiveness through @Primary test beans (the subject extractor + an in-process OpaClient that mirrors the rego) rather than a second filter chain. Guard the app's FilterRegistrationBean<AbacFilter> with @ConditionalOnBean(AbacFilter.class) so it is never created with a null filter when the starter is disabled.

name: Dictionary governance verb: team:define-tags (owner + admin), reusing the dogfooded capability ladder
description: Curating a team's tag dictionary is a MANAGEMENT capability, not a resource write. Add a 'team:define-tags' verb to the TeamRoleCapabilities ladder for BOTH owner and administrator (admins curate the vocabulary writers assign from — governed-tag model), distinct from owner-only 'team:define-roles' which shapes the access ladder itself. Because the verb shares the 'team:' prefix and team.rego is generic (verb in role_definition.permissions['team']), the policy needs NO logic change — only the ladder + doc + opa-test additions. The capability flows owner/admin -> EffectiveRoleService.managementRole -> TeamRoleDefinitionSupplier -> the dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize. Keep the three layers separate: define = governance (this verb); assign = a normal resource write (no new capability); the grant = the role + the Rego match.

title: required_tags never gate READ navigation of the governing root by default; catalogs taggable with no extra param
rationale: A role-level attribute filter must not void the explicit team binding on the resource the team-target names — the lockout protected only shell metadata (per-row filtering below the root is unchanged). Knob = OPA data (policy-owned semantic, folds clean in partial eval), NOT application.yaml (would need new starter input API). Absent flag = strict (fail-closed). No taggability param (avoids a 2x2 config matrix; UI copy handles the root-tags-look-inert confusion). Per-type required_tags = the rejected-for-now expressive alternative.

name: Two-layer authorization: coarse gateway + fine app check
description: Split authorization into a coarse gateway layer (e.g. APISIX calling OPA to check the request maps to a known route + the subject holds the permission CATEGORY) and a fine application layer (the service runs an ABAC check on the concrete resource's attributes). The gateway is an explicit allow-list (default deny): every new endpoint path needs its own validator + allow rule, or it is rejected regardless of role. The app layer checks individual action permissions against the loaded resource. Both must agree; a new action needs updating in both places.

title: Team access is app-resolved first (HTTP RoleDefinitionSupplier); ReBAC-in-Rego deferred
rationale: For the user-management-service (Phase 4 team abstraction), authorization is APP-RESOLVED: the user-service owns teams + role definitions + grants (TeamMembership = the binding) and exposes an internal GET /effective-role?userId&resourceType&resourceId that walks user->memberships->team(matching team-target)->bound RoleDefinition server-side. The catalog app's HTTP-backed RoleDefinitionSupplier (app code, NOT a library change) calls it and returns a core.RoleDefinition; the catalog still passes role_definition in the OPA input exactly as Phase 3 did. Chosen over (a) token-claim delivery (token-size/freshness bound, pushes authority into Keycloak) and (b) ReBAC-in-Rego (push the team/membership/grant graph into OPA data and do the 'member-of team AND team has-role-on resource' Zanzibar userset join in the policy). ReBAC is the more elegant end state and the strongest portfolio piece but a bigger lift + different data-distribution model, so it is DEFERRED to a new Phase 7 where it can be compared against the app-resolved path. Key reason app-resolved ships first: it reuses the Phase-3 spine with ZERO wire change (the RoleDefinitionSupplier SPI already returns a RoleDefinition) and is a single-bean swap of the demo supplier. The model encodes role != grant (separate RoleDefinition + TeamMembership), fixed system roles (owner/administrator/member/viewer) + team-scoped custom roles, owner-on-create (atomic), transfer-ownership, the Kubernetes no-self-escalation subset rule, revocation-via-membership, and authorize-the-actor. The user-service dogfoods the starter by securing its own management API with @OpaPreAuthorize. Planned in docs/to-do/planning/USER-MANAGEMENT-SERVICE.

description: When a slice ADDS a file to a mirrored bundle, the existing drift guard does not automatically cover it. 6.7 made team.rego category-driven, so the user-mgmt service bundle gained verbatim copies of permissions.rego + permission_categories.json (the mirror obligation). But the CI 'must not drift' step in .github/workflows/ci.yml diffed only the PRE-EXISTING two files (team.rego + team_test.rego), and the U9 PermissionCategoriesParityTest pinned the Java EXPANSION to the INFRA json only (never read the service-bundle copy). So the two NEW mirror files could drift from infra silently — diff was clean at ship time, but nothing enforced it. The slice's own ★ gates + the full e2e did NOT catch it (the byte-identity was verified ad-hoc with diff, not by an enforced guard); the post-run multi-lens deep-review's COMPLETENESS CRITIC found it (refutation-only would not have — no lens generated it; it is an unswept sibling of the guard, exactly the missing-wiring class the critic exists to widen into).
resolution: When a slice grows a mirrored bundle (or any 'these N files must stay byte-identical' set), GROW THE GUARD in the same slice: (a) make the CI diff step a loop over ALL bundle files, not a hardcoded pair — for f in team.rego team_test.rego permissions.rego permission_categories.json; do diff -u infra/.../$f service/.../$f; done; (b) add a local unit drift guard (PermissionCategoriesParityTest.serviceBundlePolicyCopiesAreByteIdenticalToInfra reads BOTH copies and asserts equal) so drift breaks ./gradlew build without Docker. Defense-in-depth: CI catches it in PR, the unit test on every build. General rule: a 'mirror obligation' documented in an ADR/QA but enforced only by an ad-hoc diff is a latent drift bug the moment the mirrored set grows — the guard must enumerate the set programmatically, not by hardcoded filename.

name: Team-based resource access models across cloud platforms (AWS/Heroku/GitHub/GCP/K8s/OpenFGA)
description: Cross-platform study for designing a team-scoped ABAC-over-OPA model (creator->auto-owner->team->team-scoped roles->resource grant). KEY DISTINCTION every platform makes: role != grant/binding. A ROLE (GCP role, K8s ClusterRole, GitHub repo role) is a reusable named permission set; a GRANT/BINDING is {principal + role + scoped resource}. GCP names it cleanly: binding = principal + role + (resource) + optional condition. MODELS: AWS=account owns the resource (not the user); within-account access is the UNION of identity-based + resource-based policies, cross-account needs BOTH (two-key). Heroku=3 fixed team roles (admin/member/collaborator) + per-app view/deploy/operate/manage grants (coarse role + fine per-resource grant). GitHub=team GRANTS repo access (read/triage/write/maintain/admin); nested teams inherit parent access; join team -> inherit its repo perms; transfer-ownership makes new owner admin + old owner collaborator; orphaned repo needs Support. GCP=binding on a resource node, role inherited additively DOWN org->folder->project->resource; custom roles only at project/org (not folder). K8s=Role(namespaced) vs ClusterRole(global), RoleBinding can reference a ClusterRole to REUSE a global definition but SCOPE it to one namespace ('definition global, binding scoped'); anti-escalation rule: you cannot create a role/binding granting MORE than you already hold unless you have explicit escalate/bind. OpenFGA/Zanzibar(ReBAC)=tuples (user,relation,object); 'team is editor of folder' is the userset tuple (team:X#member, editor, folder:Y) -> every member auto-inherits; 'team grants access' is LITERALLY a userset. SYNTHESIS for our model: (1) owner-on-create = atomically write (creator,owner,resource) in the same tx as resource creation + keep a team-admin fallback so a resource is never grant-less; (2) prefer resource->team INDIRECTION over direct ownership (O(1) revocation, central audit, no orphaning) with an owner ROLE held by a person on top + first-class transfer-ownership; (3) ship immutable system roles (owner/administrator/member[/viewer]) for the common case, team-scoped CUSTOM role defs as gated opt-in; (4) authorize HYBRID in Rego: RBAC role->perms map in data, ReBAC-style join (subject member-of team AND team has-role-on resource) for 'team grants access', ABAC predicate owner==subject for bootstrap; OPA expresses all three over input+data. PITFALLS: self-escalation (use the K8s subset rule), confused deputy (authorize the ACTOR of a grant not the service identity), role explosion (keep roles reusable, scope via bindings, use ReBAC indirection not per-relationship roles), revocation propagation (membership = single source of truth so checks re-derive; invalidate caches on membership change). Full cited report + URLs lives in the USER-MANAGEMENT-SERVICE planning notes.

B4 fallback removal (T1) broke EVERY type-level @OpaPreAuthorize gate under the http (membership) role-source profile, not just the list rows the design anticipated. A type-level gate (category:list, category:create, category:assign-tags-for-create, product:list, product:create) declares resourceType but NO resourceId (the child has no id yet / a list has no instance). The manager then does roleDefinitionSupplier.lookup(sub, 'category', NULL); HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier returns empty for a null resourceId -> NO role_definition at the gate. Pre-B4 these gates passed via the realm-role FALLBACK (granted if not has_role_definition; catalog-editor in roles). T1 removed it -> every type-level gate denies a legitimate catalog member -> 403 on list/create/tag-on-create. ~8 e2e matrices create categories/products in setup and broke. The 00-DESIGN §5 blast-radius analysis MISSED this (it only flagged catalog:create) because it reasoned about the filter RESIDUAL, not the coarse type-level GATE that every list/create rides under http.
resolution: Add an @OpaPreAuthorize roleResourceType/roleResourceId override (SpEL) that resolves the caller's ROLE on a governing PARENT (the catalogId path param) for a type-level child gate, while the DECIDED resource (the queried policy document, keyed on resourceType) stays the child. Wire it on category/product list+create + the TagDecisionGate.requireCategoryAssignTagsForCreate (which needed a catalogId param added). The EXISTING category 'list_inheritable_grant' clause (allow if {not input.resource.id; not denied; verb in effective_actions(role, inheritable_ancestor)}) is VERB-AGNOSTIC — it already covers create/assign-tags/list once the role resolves on the parent; product needed the same clause added (it had none, being a leaf). A non-member resolves no role -> still denied (isolation preserved). The override is fail-closed (declared-but-unresolvable -> deny, never the type-level lookup). Lesson for planning: when removing a policy fallback, audit EVERY type-level gate (list AND create AND tag-on-create), not just the list-rows residual — the fallback was load-bearing for the coarse gate, which has no role under app-resolved roles. opa test 188->197; security 133.

description: 6.5 e2e (E1b): a deny-overrides cell flipped (DELETE 204 instead of 403) because the fixture role granted WRITE on the CATALOG as well as the category - inherited_grant consults the ANCESTOR type's effective set, where delete was not denied, so the category-type denial was bypassed via the 5.5-A inheritance path. This is the DESIGNED semantic (00-DESIGN 2.9: per-type subtraction; effective_actions(role, ancestor_type) on the inherited path), not a policy bug.
resolution: Denials are PER TYPE and do not veto other grant paths: to fence an action subtree-wide, deny it on EVERY granted type or use a wildcard denial key '*' (denied_for is wildcard-aware). When writing deny-overrides fixtures/cells, grant the category-bearing type ONLY what the cell needs - an ancestor-type WRITE legitimately covers subtree actions. Documented in the PERMISSION-MODEL guide (T8) as the adopter-facing subtlety.

title: Dynamic tag dictionary: three separable layers (definition / assignment / requirement), match-in-Rego, global+team-scoped
rationale: Phase-4.5 design, decided with the maintainer. Generalizes the source platform's tag machinery (study-only @AutoTag/TagDictionary/ResourceTag) but IMPROVES on it: the source only has compile-time system tag KEYS (no user-managed, team-scoped, runtime-defined tags). The clean design separates three concerns the source tangles in one package: (1) tag DEFINITION = a dictionary entry {key, scope, valueType(STRING|ENUM), cardinality(SINGLE|MULTI), allowedValues?}; scope is GLOBAL(system, seeded, immutable) vs TEAM(owner/admin-defined) — reusing the EXACT system-vs-team partial-unique-index pattern already shipped for role definitions (team_id IS NULL). (2) tag ASSIGNMENT = attaching validated values to a (sub-)resource on create/update, stored in the existing ResourceTags JSONB (which already supports scalar AND array => single/multi free). (3) tag REQUIREMENT = a role definition carries required-tags + a match mode ANY_OF/ALL_OF; a user carrying the role gains access when the resource's tags satisfy it. DECISIONS: match is evaluated IN REGO (some in = any-of/exists, every = all-of/forall) — the industry-standard semantics (AWS ForAnyValue:/ForAllValues:, Cerbos any/all/none, OpenFGA conditions) — making tags actually grant access and leading into Phase-7 ReBAC; dictionary is BOTH global+team-scoped; owner/admin DEFINE the dictionary (management capability) while members ASSIGN values (normal write), matching Databricks governed-tags/AWS tag-policy governance. This turn produces the design/decomposition package only (workflow-as-artifact); implementation runs separately.

name: First consumer feature request: cross-team supervisor/read-all role (research queued)
description: 2026-07-13, post-1.0-publish: the corp IdP consumer's PM requested the FIRST consumer-driven feature — a supervisor/top-manager who sits above the managers of catalog teams and must log in to SEE ALL CATALOGS to track cross-team activity (read-oriented, transcends team membership). THE TENSION: Slice B4 (mx-6f551d) made team membership the SOLE access path to the catalog root list — coarse catalog:list gate DROPPED, GovernedScopeResolver (id IN governed-ids else denyAll) is the only authority, fail-closed to empty; catalog.rego filter is role-def-only, no subject-roles fallback (mx-078a8e). So a supervisor who is a member of nothing sees NOTHING by design. The feature is precisely to PIERCE that isolation READ-only + auditably WITHOUT reintroducing the realm-role fallback B4 removed (=fail-open backdoor). NOT researched yet — a phase-① scoping brief is written at ai-engineering-vault/04-Open-Source/spring-boot-starter-opa-abac/Research-Supervisor-Read-All-Role.md enumerating 4 candidate framings ((a) tenant-wide READ role via permission categories, (b) super-team auto-membership, (c) GovernedScopeResolver widening — the tempting-but-distrust shortcut = 2nd authority beside membership, (d) org-hierarchy node + inheritable READ grant reusing mx-9dbdc1/mx-cdbfe4) and 5 forks; the KEYSTONE fork to clarify with the PM = flat read-ALL vs supervised-SUBTREE (supervisor->manager->team chain hint favors (d)). Next session: clarify fork 3 -> grill-me -> ADR/design -> prototype a supervisor persona on the demo rig -> decompose -> implement. Consumer rationale stays OUT of committed repo files (clean-room); memory opa-abac-first-consumer-supervisor-req + the vault brief only.

name: Delta-dispatched decisions must version-bind EVERY downstream mutation branch
description: The 6.5 delta dispatch decides WHICH authorization questions to ask from a pre-lock read; the no-reparent branch carried that read's @Version into save (drift -> optimistic 409), but the RE-PARENT branch replaced the entity with a fresh post-lock re-read (entityManager.clear() + findById after the native path rewrite) — absorbing any racer that committed in the window (which contains the slow tag-validation HTTP call) and silently overwriting it on the final save, including across the very WRITE/TAG boundary the dispatch decided (deep-review Critical, fixed in 136e826). Fix shape: pass the decision snapshot (the pre-dispatch entity, a Versioned) INTO the locked service; VersionGuard.requireUnchanged(snapshot, lockedRow) right after the FOR UPDATE read, before any write -> VersionConflictException -> the uniform 409 STATE_CONFLICT. Review rule: when a handler's decisions are computed on a loaded entity, trace every mutation branch downstream — any branch that re-loads (locked or not) has DISCARDED the binding unless it explicitly re-checks the decision-time version under its own protection.

name: Supervisor req REFINEMENT: unit-bounded by reporting structure, not flat read-all
description: Refines the prior supervisor/read-all reference (2026-07-13, same session). The PM clarified: the supervisor sees NOT all catalogs but only HIS UNIT's — the catalogs driven by 'his' employees. Boundary = the ORGANIZATIONAL/REPORTING structure (supervisor -> his employees -> the teams they own -> those catalogs); a different supervisor sees a different set. RESOLVES the flat-vs-subtree keystone fork -> supervised-SUBTREE scoped by reporting relation. This kills the flat framings (tenant-wide READ role, super-team auto-membership = over-grant). NEW CENTRAL FORK opened: the starter has NO model of 'who reports to whom' — a new attribute source. Since the corp consumer is an IdP project, the reporting/org structure likely already lives in Keycloak (groups / manager attribute) -> resolve the supervised set from the DIRECTORY (possibly extending the ADR-0020 UserDirectory port) rather than inventing a resource hierarchy. LEADING DESIGN = framing (c): a reporting-driven GovernedScopeResolver extension that, for a supervisor subject, returns the catalog-id set DERIVED from the reporting graph (his people -> their catalogs) — keeping governed-scope the ONE authority B4 established, extended one relation past membership, fail-closed + re-derived live + READ-only (widening confined to the list/scope path, provably cannot reach per-resource write auth). (d) org-hierarchy is the fallback if org==resource-tree. Remaining forks for grill-me: transitivity (direct reports vs full subtree), supervisor-claim source (who IS a supervisor), read-only ceiling composition, freshness/invalidation. Full brief updated: ai-engineering-vault/04-Open-Source/spring-boot-starter-opa-abac/Research-Supervisor-Read-All-Role.md. Next session: clarify with PM WHERE the reporting structure lives, then grill-me -> ADR -> prototype a supervisor persona + reporting fixture on the demo rig -> decompose.

title: user-management-service is layered (dedicated service/) where the catalog stays flat; hand-written mapper, no MapStruct, no facade
rationale: Phase-4 user-management-service internal structure, decided with the maintainer. The catalog app is deliberately FLAT (config/domain/web; controllers call repositories directly; the only service, ProductService, exists solely for the optimistic-lock concurrency demo) to teach 'no ceremony needed to use the starter'. The user-service makes exactly ONE justified divergence: a dedicated @Transactional service/ package (TeamService, RoleDefinitionService, MembershipService, EffectiveRoleResolver). Rationale: its core operations are inherently CROSS-ENTITY and TRANSACTIONAL — owner-on-create (Team + owner TeamMembership in one tx), transfer-ownership (atomic up/down), the no-self-escalation subset rule (read actor effective role -> validate target -> write), and effective-role resolution (the membership walk). These cannot live in a controller without becoming a design smell; the catalog had none of these, so flat was right there. DECIDED AGAINST: (a) MapStruct — keep a hand-written static UserMgmtMapper mirroring the catalog CatalogMapper, for sibling-consistency in a repo meant to be READ, to avoid a third codegen stage alongside the OpenAPI generator, and because ~4 flat DTOs do not earn MapStruct nesting/bulk-copy strengths; (b) a facade layer — correct overkill for a single multi-aggregate read (effective-role resolution); the service/ layer IS that orchestration point, so a facade would be pure-delegation lasagna. Keep the service clean so a facade is a trivial LATER insertion if Phase 5 brings read-side orchestration (batch eval / list filtering). Principle: build the seam, not the layer. Net: user-service = config/domain/SERVICE/web — exactly one new package vs the catalog, every addition earned by the domain.

name: uq_team_target makes a catalog one-team-governed (schema-level squat partial-guard)
description: The user-management-service 'team' table has a UNIQUE constraint uq_team_target on (target_type, target_id): a given resource (e.g. a catalog) can be governed by AT MOST ONE team. Surfaced in B4 T3 when an IT tried to create two teams on the same catalog id -> DataIntegrityViolationException. Consequences: (1) EffectiveRoleService.governedTargets(subject, resourceType) — which walks subject->user->memberships->teams filtered by target_type and collects target_ids — is naturally DISTINCT by id for the realistic data shape; the LinkedHashSet dedup in it is defensive belt-and-braces, not load-bearing. (2) IMPORTANT FOR B4 T7 (the squat check): part of target-squatting protection is ALREADY enforced by this constraint — you cannot create a SECOND team on a catalog another user already owns/governs (the insert fails). The B4 ResourceOwnershipResolver check (T5-T7) therefore guards the remaining hole: the FIRST team-create on a catalog you did not create (no team exists yet, so uq_team_target doesn't fire) — the ownership check verifies the caller's sub == the catalog's created_by before allowing createTeam on the public/gateway path; /internal/bootstrap bypasses. New endpoint GET /internal/governed-targets?subject&resourceType -> 200 [uuid,...] (empty array, NEVER 204, = governs nothing) is /internal-only (permitAll, in-network, NOT gateway-routed in T8).

title: 6.5 decomposition pinned five contract semantics the design left implicit
rationale: The recurring planning-gap class is 'an externally-visible semantic left unpinned pauses the run' (mx-7e0a17); decomposing PERMISSION-CATEGORIES surfaced five and pinned them in 01-DECOMPOSITION's preamble rather than mid-run: (1) authoring violations -> 422 with NEW UserMgmtErrorCode ROLE_DEFINITION_INVALID + the closed OpenAPI errorCode enum swept in the same commit, while ALL assignment-gate rejections (level, senior bound, assignable subset, AND an OPA outage during the verdict) keep the one existing 422 ROLE_SUBSET_VIOLATION shape - outage deliberately indistinguishable from not-assignable (fail-closed by indistinguishability); (2) the pinned TAG-without-WRITE-can-relabel cell is unreachable with a static @OpaPreAuthorize on PUT, so update endpoints move to delta-aware dispatch via an annotated gate bean (content->update, tags->assign-tags, both->both, empty->update conservative) - manager seam + 5.97 cache reused, zero library change; (3) the nine-runner payload migration is a mechanical rule (read->[READ], read+write->[READ,WRITE,TAG] because pre-6.5 write implied tag-setting - same principle as the realm-fallback mapping; +roleLevel 10/20) that must preserve every pinned cell; (4) the stale-flat-role e2e cell seeds via direct DB INSERT because the authoring API now rejects flat tokens by design; (5) missing/non-numeric role_level on either assignment snapshot rejects, never 0-and-pass.

description: After splitting team:manage into fine verbs (T3) and recasting TeamRoleCapabilities to category tokens (T2), every user-mgmt membership/tag/transfer IT went red — NOT because the app was wrong, but because AbacTestConfig.inProcessTeamOpaClient() is an in-process Java MIRROR of team.rego (the ITs run WITHOUT an OPA container; the secured chain calls this stub for the dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize gate). The mirror still did the OLD raw match granted.contains(verb), so once managementRole emitted [READ,CONTROL,TAG] it denied every now-fine verb (add-member not literally in the token list). Also one IT (viewerCannotManage) encoded the OLD contract (reader GET /members -> 403) that 6.7 intentionally loosens to 200 (list-members in READ) — a known intended break, like the permissions_test READ-expansion break.
resolution: Any slice that changes team.rego's decision shape MUST update AbacTestConfig.inProcessTeamOpaClient() in lockstep (it's a parallel implementation of the policy for the no-container IT path) — and grep the existing ITs for cells that assert the OLD allow/deny contract. Recast the mirror to expand category tokens through PermissionCategories.EXPANSION (the U9-parity-pinned table — reuse it so IT math can't drift from the OPA data file) minus denied_actions, plus the owner-only-by-code fence (verb in {define-roles,transfer-ownership} AND code=="owner"). This is a build-breaker that lands in the SAME ticket as the verb split, not deferred. The two-axis MembershipGateIT escalation cells pass UNCHANGED through the renamed verbs (the gates are orthogonal).

title: Keep the tag access requirement on the RoleDefinition (AWS-IAM-style), not on the resource (Keycloak-style)
rationale: Deep-research (NIST SP 800-162, AWS IAM ABAC docs, Keycloak Authorization Services, XACML; 24/25 claims verified 3-0) confirmed both are valid ABAC but they differ decisively for THIS repo. Subject-side (today): requiredTags+matchMode live on the role; resources carry plain tag VALUES; matchMode ALL_OF/ANY_OF == AWS ForAllValues/ForAnyValue. It is FAIL-CLOSED by construction (no role def -> DENY_ALL; no requiredTags -> vacuously-true full reach; tags only SUBTRACT) and composes natively with the Phase-5 partial-eval row filter (requirement -> residual WHERE over the tags JSONB). Resource-side (Keycloak: a permission attaches policies to the protected resource) is intuitive for resource owners BUT its natural default 'untagged resource is open to everyone' is a documented FAIL-OPEN (AWS warns ForAllValues is vacuously true over an empty/absent key — the same hazard) which conflicts with the repo's load-bearing fail-closed invariant.

title: 6.7 control-plane categorization: CONTROL category + two-axis separation (verb vs escalation gate)
rationale: Phase 6.7 phase-① grill-me (2026-06-15) settled the control-plane vocabulary shape. ONE shared category vocabulary (not a separate control-plane taxonomy): team:* verbs fold into permission_categories.json. The full split of the coarse 'manage' verb into membership fine-actions makes CONTROL a REFINABLE category (the catalog's WRITE pattern). GROUPING: READ -> [view, list, list-members] (any team member can now list the roster — an externally-visible behavior change from today's manager-only listing); CONTROL -> [add-member, change-role, remove-member] (membership mutation, deny-refinable: deny remove-member = onboard/retitle but never remove). define-tags STAYS under TAG (already in the table). define-roles + transfer-ownership remain OWNER-ONLY FENCES outside the category system (ADR 0007's escalation-via-authoring branch stays pruned). THE 6.7 PRINCIPLE — two orthogonal axes: (1) the VERB category (CONTROL + deny-overrides) decides WHICH KINDS of membership acts a role may perform; (2) the SHIPPED escalation gates in MembershipService (cross-tier strict <, senior subset-on-effective, target-tier, owner-protection) decide ON WHOM and TO WHAT TIER. 6.7 touches ONLY axis 1; axis 2 is an invariant, untouched. Consequence: holding add-member does NOT imply change-role (independent fine actions); and whatever verbs you hold, the gates still forbid acting on anyone above your tier or promoting past your own ceiling. Single-expansion-home teaching artifact preserved: team.rego will call effective_actions(role_def, 'team') exactly like catalog.rego.

title: Coarse-grained permission categories (READ/WRITE/TAG/GRANT) + five-tier role-level ceiling model + deny-overrides; subset rule scoped to the senior tier only
rationale: Designed via grill-me + web research (AWS/Azure/GCP/GitHub/Heroku/K8s). For the catalog domain (Catalog->Category->Product), the permission model: (1) FOUR coarse CATEGORIES that expand to fine actions — READ {view,list}, WRITE {create,update,delete}, TAG {define-tags,assign-tags}, GRANT {assign-roles}. Named GRANT (not MANAGE — MANAGE is ambiguous between manage-config and manage-access; every platform fences 'grant access to others' as a separate top capability: AWS Permissions-management, Azure Owner-vs-Contributor NotActions Microsoft.Authorization/*, GCP setIamPolicy, GitHub Admin, K8s admin-creates-RoleBindings). TAG (not CURATE) for plainness + matches AWS 'Tagging' access level + the shipped team:define-tags (ADR 0004). (2) GRANT MODEL = categories-only (NO a-la-carte individual-action grants) + DENY-OVERRIDES on top (Azure Actions/NotActions): effective_actions(type) = expand(granted_categories) \ denied_actions; allow if requested in effective. Denial is a global hard veto applied last. Rationale: survives new actions gracefully (a new action added to WRITE is auto-included unless denied — Azure's documented reason), lossless UI round-trip (store intent=categories not effect=actions), one grant shape. (3) EXPANSION lives in OPA: store category tokens; expansion table in OPA data (editable, no redeploy); Rego does expand-minus-deny — the teachable 'OPA expands coarse->fine' demo. (4) role_level = a PERMISSION CEILING/TEMPLATE, not free integer: owner picks level -> the ceiling categories auto-check and LOCK in the UI (higher disabled/uncheckable) -> owner refines DOWNWARD only via deny-overrides. FIVE authored tiers + owner reserved: reader(10) ceiling {READ}; member(20) {READ,WRITE,TAG}; senior(25) {READ,WRITE,TAG} + a constrained assign-members power; administrator(30) {READ,WRITE,TAG,GRANT}; owner=reserved root (authors role DEFINITIONS, assigns anything, transfer-ownership). (5) TWO FENCES (invariants): define-roles (authoring) = OWNER-ONLY, never a category, never delegatable (decided against delegating to admins — complicates trust analysis hugely); GRANT (assign roles) tops out at ADMINISTRATOR — senior canNOT hold/assign GRANT, so senior can only onboard member-or-lower roles and self-replication of assignment power is structurally impossible. (6) TWO ASSIGNMENT GATES, each one job: role_level strict '<' = cross-tier seniority (admin can't add admin); SUBSET RULE on effective (expanded-minus-denied) permission sets = used ONLY at the senior tier to order which member-roles a senior may hand out. KEY: subset is OPTIONAL complexity that exists to buy EXACTLY ONE feature (the senior delegate persona) — drop senior and you can drop subset and run on role_level alone. Personas (dev team): PM=owner, lead/architect=admin, senior-dev=senior, mid-dev/analyst=member, stakeholder=reader. ADDITIVITY: reuses the shipped role_level attribute (owner40/admin30/member20/viewer10 seeds) and the {type:[verbs]} permissions shape (a category token is new, a plain action token still works). The effective_actions expansion is reused at BOTH decision time and assignment-subset time (one function). Leads to ADR 0007 (planned, Phase ~6/7) + user stories in USER-STORIES.

description: A permission-vocabulary migration swept only the annotation strings: T6 migrated every @OpaPreAuthorize action but missed the two Java components that EMIT or CONSUME the old tokens — DemoRoleDefinitionSupplier (still emitted flat read/write; the default demo profile denied everything under the 6.5 policies via the clean-cut ∅-expansion) and CategoryListAuthorizer→SubtreeSpecResolver (asked for flat 'read' which no category-token role carries; the 5.5-B subtree widening went silently dead — every inheritable list degraded to the batch recheck, CORRECT rows masking the regression, so all e2e stayed green).
resolution: Deep-review fix 136e826: demo supplier now emits READ / READ+WRITE+TAG mirroring the realm fallback; the list authorizer passes the READ token behind a conservative pre-gate (no denials on the root type, no required_tags — token membership can't see either and an over-widened subtreeSpec would LEAK rows since it is OR-ed with the residual); CategoryListWideningParityTest pins 'list expands from READ and only READ' to the OPA data table. Decomposition rule for the next vocabulary change: enumerate every Java emitter/consumer of the old vocabulary (suppliers, authorizers, capability maps, resolver verbs), grep-derived, in the ticket itself — annotation sweeps are not enough, and a fail-closed degrade can hide the miss behind green tests.

name: Hybrid assignment gates: Java tier compares under the row lock + an app-side OPA entrypoint client, fail-closed
description: The 6.5 delegation shape: assignment authority = (1) a Java cross-tier level compare (actorLevel > candidateLevel from attributes.role_level; unreadable level REJECTS, never 0-and-pass) + (2) at the senior tier only, an OPA subset-on-effective verdict (data.role.assignable over RAW row snapshots - the policy's shared effective_actions does wildcard+denial math, so Java never reimplements set algebra). Both gates and snapshots read AFTER lockTeam in the same tx (decide-under-protection; latch IT proves the stale snapshot would have passed). The OPA call needs an app-side RestClient (OpaClient exposes no arbitrary entrypoint): short timeouts, any error/non-2xx/missing result -> false. Level gates run FIRST so the verdict is never consulted when the tier already rejects (ITs assert zero stub calls via a counting in-process HttpServer). Gotcha pair: (a) a custom role at an admin/senior LEVEL has the authoring ceiling but NO live manage capability (TeamRoleCapabilities keys by CODE) - tier-with-denial cells are only constructible at service level; (b) a TOCTOU latch cell must pick tiers where the STALE snapshot passes, or the outcome cannot distinguish stale-read from lock-read.

name: Delta-aware gate dispatch: conditional decisions via an annotated gate bean, reachability-scoped
description: To enforce a TAG/WRITE-style boundary that a static @OpaPreAuthorize cannot express (TAG-without-WRITE relabels but never edits), move the update handler's authorization to CONDITIONAL calls on a dedicated gate bean whose methods each carry their own @OpaPreAuthorize (manager seam + 5.97 request cache reused; calls must cross the bean boundary - never self-invocation). Dispatch: content delta -> :update; tags delta (RAW request map vs entity tags, null=empty, clearing counts - raw compare can only OVER-ask) -> :assign-tags; both -> both; EMPTY delta -> :update (conservative). Decisions precede the version guard, the tag validation (no 422-vocabulary leak to unauthorized callers), and any mutation. THREE knock-ons to plan for: (1) scope the dispatch to types whose REST requests actually carry tags - an unreachable assign-tags branch is dead code; (2) the handler's missing-id answer flips 403->404 (the annotated-resourceId precondition moves off the handler; the load precedes the dispatch); (3) any aspect-injected gate-window race IT pinned on that handler loses its window - move the cell to a still-statically-annotated sibling.

title: Phase 6.5 permission categories: the ten pinned forks
rationale: Clean cut: zero external adopters makes back-compat machinery pure cost (legacy aliases would live in the expansion table forever and publish dirty). Hybrid gates: the team-row lock and decide-under-protection live in Java (B3), while the expansion table must stay editable-without-redeploy in OPA data — splitting the gates along that line keeps one runtime source for effective_actions with no TOCTOU. Deferring define-tags keeps the Q1 scope boundary honest (the dictionary endpoints are control-plane-gated) and avoids a silent default widening (member ceiling includes TAG).

name: App-resolved effective-role: one resolver, two projections, pluggable team-target matcher
description: The user-management-service resolves a caller's effective role from LIVE team membership (membership is the single source of truth — always re-derive, never denormalize, so removing a member revokes immediately). One EffectiveRoleService is the single seam, returning TWO projections of the same membership: (1) a MANAGEMENT role (permissions['team'] = a capability ladder owner>admin>member/viewer) consumed by the service's OWN dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize when securing the management API; (2) a RESOURCE role (the bound role's stored permissions, with a wildcard '*' resource type expanded to the concrete team-target type) returned by the INTERNAL GET /internal/effective-role?userId&resourceType&resourceId endpoint that the catalog's HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier consumes. The resolve endpoint is internal-only (permitAll under /internal/**, never gateway-fronted — an in-network attribute source), returns the raw core.RoleDefinition wire shape (code/attributes/permissions) so the catalog deserializes directly, and answers 204 (empty, NOT an error) on no-match so the catalog supplier maps it to Optional.empty() and the policy default-denies (fail-closed). Resource->team matching is a pluggable TeamTargetMatcher SPI (ExactTeamTargetMatcher default = exact (type,id) match; a hierarchy-walking matcher is an additive Phase-5 swap). The 'userId' param is the IdP subject (sub) the catalog forwards, not the internal user UUID.

title: 6.7 OPA wiring: mirror permissions.rego + permission_categories.json into the user-mgmt service bundle; keep TAG intact, add CONTROL only
rationale: 6.7 phase-① (2026-06-15). TWO OPA bundles: runtime = single shared OPA container mounting infra/opa/policies/ (has team.rego + permissions.rego + permission_categories.json + role.rego + catalog policies — all co-loaded, so team.rego CAN reference data.permissions.effective_actions at runtime today). But example-user-management-service/src/main/resources/opa/policies/ is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for team.rego and holds ONLY team.rego + team_test.rego — its isolated 'opa test' (14/14) would BREAK once team.rego calls data.permissions.effective_actions. DECISION (Option A): copy permissions.rego + permission_categories.json VERBATIM into the service bundle so the dogfood team.rego resolves effective_actions and opa test stays self-contained per-module. Consistent with the already-accepted duplication model (README: service bundle = source of truth, infra = a mounted copy). PROOF OBLIGATION / two-copy gotcha to pin for the run: the CONTROL category + the list-members addition to READ must land in BOTH permission_categories.json copies (infra + service); permissions.rego copied verbatim. FINAL 6.7 CATEGORY TABLE: READ->[view,list,list-members]; WRITE->[create,update,delete] (unchanged); TAG->[define-tags,assign-tags] (UNCHANGED — define-tags stays in TAG, kept there to avoid a 2nd new category + shipped-catalog churn; per-plane inertness is intentional: define-tags live only on team, assign-tags only on catalog); GRANT->[assign-roles] (unchanged); CONTROL->[add-member,change-role,remove-member] (the ONE new category). define-tags re-gating is purely mechanical: team:define-tags annotation unchanged, now granted via the TAG token in owner/admin ladder + expanded by team.rego; behavior identical (owner/admin curate, others 403); senior correctly stays WITHOUT define-tags (holds CONTROL not TAG).

name: Role provenance stamp: confine ancestor inheritance to membership-derived roles
description: SUPERVISED-SCOPE part 0 / ADR 0031. A SYNTHESIZED role (one built in code rather than resolved from a membership — the supervised read scope's catalog:[READ], and the tiered/elevated roles of later slices) is INDISTINGUISHABLE in policy input from a wildcard-expanded membership role: resourceRole() expands a stored '*' to the requested type, so both arrive as {catalog:[tokens]}. No structural test separates them, so a MARKER IS MANDATORY. The shape: (1) RoleDefinition.attributes.provenance carries a value vocabulary ('membership' | 'supervised' | one per future synthesized role) — it rides the EXISTING generic attributes map, so the wire contract is unchanged and no envelope field is added; (2) the single construction funnel for roles reaching the leaf policies stamps it by OVERWRITE, never merge; (3) the leaf policies' inheritance clauses (inherited_grant + list_inheritable_grant, per type) gain the conjunct — NOT permissions.effective_actions, because direct grants use the same helper (the supervisor would lose its own catalog:view) and permissions.rego is byte-mirrored into the user-service bundle; (4) ABSENCE IS CLOSED, so a future synthesized role that forgets the stamp fails closed (a loud missing-access bug) rather than open; (5) DIRECT grants are untouched, which is why every shipped per-type role needs no change and why a later slice widens by naming child types explicitly. RESERVED-KEY DISCIPLINE IS TWO-SIDED: a stored role's attributes map is client-supplied through the role create/update API and copied verbatim onto the wire, so provenance must be STRIPPED on the write path AND OVERWRITTEN on the read path — with only the read path the guarantee holds merely by accident of the current call graph, and any future path returning a stored role lets a client's own provenance:'membership' buy back the inheritance. Because opa test inputs are hand-written and would stay green if the Java stopped stamping, a TEST AT THE SEAM asserting the stamp is required, not optional — if it ever stops, every member loses child access at once.

title: Value-immutability needs its own dictionary flag: is_system protects the DEFINITION, operatorManaged protects the VALUES
rationale: PRODUCTION-TIER T1 (ADR 0030 §3). The tier tag (env) must be unstrippable by the supervised population, so the dictionary needed 'values under this key are not writable through any public API'. The existing is_system flag could NOT be reinterpreted to carry it: both seeded GLOBAL keys (sensitivity, region) are is_system=true and yet FREELY ASSIGNABLE — is_system means 'the definition's shape is immutable through the API', a different question. The abac_deny precedent does not transfer either: abac_deny is protected by NOT EXISTING in the dictionary, while env must exist to be enum-validated, so the moment it is defined any tag holder could set or strip it. Hence a second, additive boolean operatorManaged (default false, so every pre-existing key is untouched), carried to the enforcing service through the internal TagDefinitionView projection — the catalog service cannot enforce what it never receives, which is why the projection gets its own over-the-wire test rather than trusting the shared toDto. Two shape rules keep it honest: (1) the flag appears in NO request schema (GLOBAL definitions have no public create path at all), and (2) the entity ships the getter WITHOUT a setter, deliberately breaking symmetry with every sibling field — an unused public mutator on the one field meaning 'not writable' is the first affordance a future caller reaches for; absence is a structural guarantee instead of a remembered rule. Trust dependency to restate wherever the default is read: untagged-defaults-to-non-production is defensible ONLY while the key has no public write path.
